title.rendered: The Lord Is My Strength and My Shield: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The Lord is your strength and your shield. Your heart trusts in Him. You are helped. And from the place of help, your heart leaps for joy and your song bursts forth in thanks.

content.rendered:
The Lord is your strength and your shield. Your heart trusts in Him. You are helped. And from the place of help, your heart leaps for joy and your song bursts forth in thanks.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, June 12, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in him, and he helps me. My heart leaps for joy, and with my song I praise him.”
Psalm 28:7 (NIV)

Today’s Message

David wrote Psalm 28 from a place of distress. The opening verses ask the Lord not to be silent. He was crying out for mercy, surrounded by the wicked, asking God to act on his behalf. And then somewhere in the middle of the prayer, the entire mood of the psalm shifts. Verse seven is what verse one becomes when faith does its work in the middle of trouble.

Watch the progression. The Lord is my strength. Notice the present tense. Not the Lord will be. Not the Lord might be. The Lord is. Right now. In the trouble. Whatever strength you have, He is it. Whatever you do not have, He has on your behalf.

The Lord is my shield. Not just my power for the offence. My protection on the defence. Behind every assault that does not destroy you stands the unseen shield of the One who has gone before you. You are not just supplied for the battle. You are covered in the battle.

My heart trusts in Him. That is the human part. The Lord supplies strength and shield. The believer supplies trust. Not heroic, dramatic trust. Just the small daily decision to lean the weight of the heart on the Lord rather than on anything else.

And He helps me. The verb is simple and the result is everything. The God who is strength and shield to a heart that trusts becomes the help that meets the actual moment.

Then comes the explosion. My heart leaps for joy. And with my song I praise Him. This is what genuine help does. It produces a song. The believer who has been quietly held by God in the middle of trouble does not need to fake worship. Worship comes out of them because they cannot help it. Joy leaps. Song bursts. Thanksgiving overflows. Not because the trouble has ended. Because the Helper has shown up. That is enough.

Wherever you are reading this from today, the same Lord David called on is your strength and your shield. Trust Him with your heart this morning. Watch Him help you through your day. And let the song come, when the song comes.

Prayer

Lord, You are my strength and my shield. Today I trust You with my whole heart. I lay down the things I have been trying to be strong about on my own. I let You be my power and my protection. Help me through this day, and let the song of joy You give me become the testimony of others around me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Lord is my strength and my shield. My heart trusts in Him, and He helps me. My heart leaps for joy. My song belongs to Him. I am not strong on my own. I am strong because He is.
